step_by_step_reasoning: The architecture was extracted by first identifying all distinct visual elements (icons and labeled services/actors) on the whiteboard. Floating text that was clearly a source for an arrow (like 'RDS S3 FTP API') was interpreted as a 'ThirdParty' actor to satisfy the 'arrow-driven edges' rule while adhering to the 'omit floating text' rule for individual nodes. Each identified component was assigned a unique ID. Subsequently, all visible arrows connecting these components were mapped as edges. The transcript was then used to enrich the `notes` field for both nodes and edges, clarifying their roles and interactions, and to confirm the logical flow of data (`flow_id` and `seq`). Conflicts between visual representation and transcript details were resolved by prioritizing the visual diagram for node and edge existence, and using the transcript for explanatory context.

graph.name: JD Power AI Cloud Data Lake Solution
graph.categories: Data Lake, Analytics, Machine Learning, Data Ingestion
graph.notes: Architecture for JD Power's AI Cloud data lake solution, designed for ingesting various data sources, cataloging, transforming, and enabling analytics and machine learning workloads.

nodes.name: Web Console User
nodes.notes: User interacting with the web console for data ingestion and system access.

nodes.name: User Authentication
nodes.notes: Authenticates users logging into the web console.

nodes.name: External Data Sources
nodes.notes: Represents various external data sources including RDS instances, S3 buckets, FTP locations, and APIs, from which JD Power ingests data.

nodes.name: Data Lake Storage
nodes.notes: Centralized storage for all ingested raw and processed data, acting as the foundation of the data lake.

nodes.name: Data Catalog & ETL
nodes.notes: Used to crawl data sources, create catalogs of data, and perform initial ETL operations, including moving data to S3.

nodes.name: Custom Crawler Trigger
nodes.notes: A serverless function that is triggered when Glue cannot process a file, initiating custom crawlers on Fargate.

nodes.name: Custom Crawlers & ML Endpoints
nodes.notes: Runs custom crawlers for special file formats not handled by Glue, and hosts Jupyter Notebook/RStudio endpoints for data scientists.

nodes.name: Ad-hoc Query & Transformation
nodes.notes: Used for most data analytical and transformation activities, including converting data to Parquet format and applying cleaning rules.

nodes.name: Data Warehouse
nodes.notes: Serves as a data warehouse, exposing transformed data to analytical platforms for dashboard creation.

nodes.name: Dashboard Platform
nodes.notes: Analytical platform where dashboards are created using data from Redshift.

nodes.name: ML Development
nodes.notes: Platform where data scientists build and train machine learning models, utilizing Fargate-provisioned environments.

edges.notes: User logs into the web console and is authenticated by Cognito.
User interaction with the data ingestion module through the web console leads to data storage in S3.
Raw data from various external sources (RDS, S3, FTP, APIs) is moved into S3 buckets.
Glue crawls data stored in S3 to create catalogs and prepare it for analysis.
Glue processes data, creates catalogs, and saves processed or cataloged data back into S3 buckets.
Once authenticated, user actions in the data ingestion module can trigger a Lambda function for custom processing.
Lambda triggers custom crawlers running on Fargate for handling special file formats that Glue cannot process natively.
Athena queries and transforms data directly from S3, performing activities like Parquet conversion and cleaning.
Athena utilizes the catalogs created by Glue to understand and query the data structure.
Transformed and cleaned data from Athena is moved to Redshift to build a data warehouse for advanced analytics.
Redshift exposes the prepared data to an analytical platform for creating dashboards and reports.
Fargate is used to provision Jupyter Notebook or RStudio endpoints, providing an environment for data scientists to work on the Machine Learning platform.
